keyVerseText: Therefore, behold, I will bring evil upon the house of Jeroboam, and will cut off from Jeroboam him that pisseth against the wall, and him that is shut up and left in Israel, and will take away the remnant of the house of Jeroboam, as a man taketh away dung, till it be all gone.
rootMeaning: The root of גָּלָל (gâlâl) is גָּלַל (gâlal), which primarily means to roll or to roll away. This root conveys the sense of something being moved or removed by rolling, which figuratively extends to the idea of cleansing or removing impurities. The noun גָּלָל thus literally refers to what is rolled away or discarded—dung—highlighting its nature as waste that is cast off and removed from the living space. This root sense enriches the common English gloss "dung" by emphasizing the action of removal and separation inherent in the term.
usageInScripture: The word גָּלָל appears only once in Scripture, consistently translated as "dung." This singular occurrence shows a focused usage that carries a clear and vivid image of filth and refuse. The consistency in translation underscores the word's strong association with impurity and waste, without any broader metaphorical extensions. This precise usage reveals the term's role in emphasizing degradation and removal within the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding גָּלָל as dung rooted in the concept of rolling away or removal deepens our grasp of biblical purity and judgment themes. Dung represents what is unclean and to be cast aside, symbolizing the consequences of sin and God's righteous judgment. The imagery reminds believers of the necessity of spiritual cleansing and the removal of sin through Christ. It also points to God's sovereign authority to remove wickedness completely, reinforcing the hope of restoration for those who trust in Him. Such a word invites reflection on holiness and the seriousness with which God treats defilement.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Kings 14:10, the phrase "as a man taketh away dung, till it be all gone" uses גָּלָל to vividly illustrate the totality of God's judgment against Jeroboam's house. The word conveys not just removal but thorough cleansing—just as dung is completely cleared away, so will the remnant of Jeroboam's lineage be cut off. This stark image highlights the severity of divine discipline and the inevitability of God's righteous purging of evil from His people.
